newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam defence official warns of "hostile forces".
newsitem.headline: Vietnam defence official warns of "hostile forces".

text.p: Vietnam must not lower its guard against hostile forces in the mistaken belief that it would reassure foreign investors, the National Assembly's defence and security committee chairman said on Friday.

"...we cannot miss the basic plot of hostile forces to eliminate the leading role of the Vietnam Communist Party and socialism, to force our country to follow the capitalist road," Dang Quan Thuy said in the Ho Chi Minh City Police newspaper.
Thuy said it was now popular to think that bolstering national defence and security could impair Hanoi's relations with other countries and make some hesitate before investing in the country.

"That opinion does not match the reality of what has happened," he said, noting that other, more developed countries in the region such as Singapore and Thailand had reinforced their defence capability.

"This has proved that even these economically developed countries still try to strengthen their military power, not thinking that it might affect their cooperative relations with other countries," he said.
Foreign investors have flooded into Vietnam since the party launched market-style reforms of its Soviet-style economy and opened doors to the outside world in the late 1980s.
However, recent signs that investment flows from abroad may be slowing have raised some concern within the government.

Thuy said consolidation of national defence and security to guard against "peaceful evolution" should go hand in hand with efforts to quicken the country's push for industrialisation and modernisation.
"Peaceful evolution" is the official buzzword used to describe what the party says is insidious subversion by forces hostile to the country's political system, ideology and culture.
